response.title: Following the River’s Flow
response.passage: The environmental club visited a local river for a science project. Since the banks were slippery, their teacher marked a viewing area on the dry path and told them not to enter the water. At an upstream marker, the students placed three small sticks in the river, one after another. A steady current carried each stick downstream past a lower marker in seconds. To check the direction, they released corks from the same spot and watched from the bank. All the corks moved toward a bend, and none traveled back toward the starting point. The students noted the markers’ positions and drew arrows on a map to show the water’s movement. Before leaving, they compared their maps, which all showed the flow heading toward the bend.

items.answer: It carried each test stick downstream past the lower marker.
distractors: It carried each test stick upstream past the higher marker.
It kept each test stick beside the starting marker.
It pushed each test stick back onto the dry path.
items.question: What did the steady current do to the test sticks?

items.answer: The river water was flowing toward the bend.
distractors: The river water was flowing back toward the starting point.
The river water was standing still near the bend.
The river water was flowing away from the lower marker.
items.question: What can the students infer from the way the corks moved?

items.answer: The club watched objects move in the river and recorded the direction of the flow.
distractors: The club entered the river to measure how deep it was at each marker.
The club tested whether sticks and corks could float upstream by themselves.
The club mapped the slippery banks so other students could avoid the path.
